summary: Sakunoshin Motoda was a scholar in religious studies. He studied at Kenyon College (~1888–1891), the University of Pennsylvania (~1893–1895), and Columbia University (~1895–1896), and held a post at Rikkyo University (~1899–1928).
Sakutaro Fujioka specialized in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1891 to 1894 and later held a post there from ~1900 to 1910.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Khenpo Appey, Ngawang Kunga Rinchen, Chogye Trichen, and Tenzin Gyatso, founded the Sakya Centre, and served as abbot at Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Sakyong Mipham works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under Chögyam Trungpa, Dilgo Khyentse, and Penor Rinpoche. He succeeded Chögyam Trungpa and served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religion. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1971–1973) under Leon Hurvitz (~1971–1975) and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1991–2017).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman specializes in Indology and linguistics. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (1979), studied under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and Shrinivasa Shastri, and held a post at UC Berkeley (attested 1996).
Sally McAra works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000), where she studied under supervisors Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.
Sally Mellick Cutler works in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1993) and served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1997).

Salomon Lefmann specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Münster, Heidelberg, Paris, and Berlin (~1861–1864, PhD) under Franz Bopp. He held posts at Heidelberg University as Extraordinariat für Sanskrit (1866), associate professor (1870), and honorary professor (1901).

Sam van Schaik is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester (~1996–2000) and held posts at the British Library (from 1999) and SOAS University of London.
Samani Pratibha Pragya specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at SOAS University of London, where she was attested as a research assistant in 2020.

Samdhong Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery and Gyuto Monastery (Geshe degree, 1970). He served as Director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from 1971 to 2001.

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Drepung, SOAS, and the University of London under David Llewellyn Snellgrove and Rolf A. Stein, later holding posts at SOAS, Collège de France, and CNRS (1980).

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned his BA at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1843–1847). He served at Bramham College (1848–1850) and as Professor of Chinese at University College London (1877; ~1877–1889).

Samuel George Frederick Brandon worked in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds (~1930–1934) and held a post at the University of Manchester from ~1951 to 1971.
Samuel Johnson was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge (~1726), and Pembroke College (1728–1731).
Samuel M. Grupper works in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Indiana University, where he studied under Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West.
Samuel Wells Williams worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1831–1832) and held a post at Yale University from ~1877 to 1884.

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at San Diego State University, attested as Professor in 1999 and as Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University in 1991 and also held an academic post there.
